newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures fell slightly on Friday as a stronger-than-expected rise in US hourly earnings in March reinforced concerns that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again in May.

Traders said although the number of US jobs created in March was smaller than feared and the downward revision to the February figures was favourable, the rise in wages was more likely to unsettle central bank officials.
"The headline looks good but overall the data is going to make the Fed nervous, the chances of another hike in May have increased," a futures trader at a French bank said.

Several traders said the overall mood remained bearish and there was still a good chance yields on 10-year French government bonds would rise to six percent from 5.95 percent currently, pushing the bond future down to around 126.70/80.
"Will it go down further? I don't know. We may have cash buyers below 127, but (the market) stinks, it can't hold the highs," the head of trading at a French brokerage said.
Traders said the initial bounce after the jobs report prompted some short covering, pushing the contract to 127.48, the high for the day.
When the US bond market focused on the hourly earnings figures and took a turn lower the French market followed breaking through support at 127.34/36 to hit a low of 127.06.
One trader said primary dealers were selling futures in anticipation of receiving allocations of 10-year OATS at the same price as at Thursday's auction to cover their positions.
The right of primary dealers to by OATs on Friday at Thursday's auction price is effectively an in-the-money call option when the market has risen in the interim.
The Treasury sold an extra 2.33 billion francs of OATs on Friday, of which 2 billion were 5.5 percent 2007 OATs.

Despite the relatively bearish environment for the long-end the French Treasury once again surpassed its monthly OAT funding target selling a total of 24.2 billion francs, above the 20-22 billion target.
The 10-year spread between French and German 10-year yields remained stable at minus eight basis points.
The French yield curve steepened slightly on Friday as the pessimism at the long-end continued to be at odds with hopes for steady, if not lower, interest rates in France.
June PIBOR climbed as high as 96.66, up four basis points, its highest level since February 28.

"We had some buying from overseas and there was a rally on the short end all over continental Europe," a trader said. "We had some decent short covering and broke through the (96.)63 level." He said there was now a chance the contract could return to 96.70.

One analyst at a French bank said hopes were growing that the Bank of France could trim its intervention rate without waiting for the Bundesbank to lower its key money market rate. The central bank's monetary policy council meets next Thursday.
The franc remained strong against the mark and set a 45-month high at 3.3653 late in the session.
